metadata.name: Startup / Product Development
metadata.purpose: Supplies an abstract execution framework the AI uses to reason about HOW to structure a product/startup-building workspace, before it generates domain-specific folders, files, and checklists. This document is never injected verbatim into generated content.
metadata.domainMatchingNote: This list is illustrative only, not an exhaustive match table. Blueprint selection must be based on the detected intent/category (e.g. classify.category === 'startup'), never on string-matching a product type against this list — the blueprint itself contains no product-specific content and must work equally well for a product-building goal not listed here.

stageRoles.purpose: Identify and clearly frame the real problem or opportunity before any solution work begins.
stageRoles.whyThisStageExists: Experienced builders know most failed products fail because the problem was never real or never understood — this stage exists to prevent solving a problem nobody has.
stageRoles.whatShouldHappen: The founder investigates who has the problem, how painful it is, what they currently do about it today, and whether it's worth solving.
stageRoles.prerequisites: None — this is the entry stage. Only the user's stated goal is required.
stageRoles.whatComesNext: Validation — once a problem is framed, it must be tested against reality before real investment.
stageRoles.skipCondition: Skippable only if the clarification answers indicate the problem was already independently validated before this workspace was created.
stageRoles.mandatoryReason: Every later stage assumes a clearly framed problem exists to build toward.
stageRoles.folderGenerationGuidelines: Rename to reflect the specific problem or opportunity space implied by the goal — never leave it as 'Discovery'. Usually one folder.
stageRoles.fileGenerationGuidelines: Introduction role frames the space; a Concept-role file captures the problem hypothesis in writing.
stageRoles.checklistGenerationPhilosophy: Tasks should investigate and frame the problem, not build anything yet.

stageRoles.purpose: Test whether the framed problem and proposed direction actually hold up against real evidence before committing resources.
stageRoles.whyThisStageExists: Experts validate before they build — untested assumptions are the single most common cause of wasted product effort.
stageRoles.whatShouldHappen: The founder gathers real signal (conversations, data, competitive research, small tests) that either confirms or challenges the Discovery-stage hypothesis.
stageRoles.prerequisites: Discovery stage complete — a clear problem hypothesis must exist to validate.
stageRoles.whatComesNext: Planning — a validated direction becomes the basis for a concrete plan.
stageRoles.skipCondition: Not skippable — even a fast, lightweight validation pass must occur before Planning.
stageRoles.mandatoryReason: Planning without validation risks building the wrong thing well.
stageRoles.folderGenerationGuidelines: One or two folders reflecting the specific validation methods the goal's domain calls for.
stageRoles.fileGenerationGuidelines: Hands-on Practice role (running the actual validation activity) paired with a Validation-role file that records findings and the resulting decision.
stageRoles.checklistGenerationPhilosophy: Tasks should produce real evidence, not rest on assumptions.

stageRoles.purpose: Turn a validated direction into a concrete, buildable plan.
stageRoles.whyThisStageExists: Experts scope before they build — a plan prevents scope creep and wasted work once building starts.
stageRoles.whatShouldHappen: The founder defines what will actually be built first, what's explicitly out of scope, and the order of work.
stageRoles.prerequisites: Validation stage complete with a clear go/no-go decision.
stageRoles.whatComesNext: Prototyping — the plan becomes a guided, low-stakes first build.
stageRoles.skipCondition: Not skippable — even a minimal plan must exist before building starts.
stageRoles.mandatoryReason: Build later assumes a defined scope and sequence exist.
stageRoles.folderGenerationGuidelines: One folder covering scope and roadmap decisions specific to the goal — never a generic 'Planning' folder, always tied to what's actually being planned.
stageRoles.fileGenerationGuidelines: A Concept-role file (the plan itself, written down) is dominant here.
stageRoles.checklistGenerationPhilosophy: Tasks should define scope and sequence, not execute the build yet.

stageRoles.purpose: Build the smallest possible version that proves the core idea works, under heavy simplification.
stageRoles.whyThisStageExists: Experts always build the cheapest possible proof before committing to the full build — this catches fundamental flaws while they're still cheap to fix.
stageRoles.whatShouldHappen: The founder builds a minimal, rough version — not production quality — focused only on proving the riskiest assumption.
stageRoles.whatComesNext: Build — once the core idea is proven, the founder invests in a real, complete version.
stageRoles.skipCondition: Skippable for goals where the core risk was already resolved in Validation, or the domain doesn't require a technical prototype.
stageRoles.mandatoryReason: Valuable risk-reduction step, but not load-bearing if the riskiest assumption is already proven.
stageRoles.folderGenerationGuidelines: One folder for the minimal proof-of-concept work, scoped tightly to the goal's riskiest assumption.
stageRoles.fileGenerationGuidelines: Hands-on Practice role dominant — this is fast, rough building, not polished Application work yet.
stageRoles.checklistGenerationPhilosophy: Tasks should be fast and rough, proving one thing at a time.

stageRoles.purpose: Build the real, complete version intended for actual use, not just a proof.
stageRoles.whyThisStageExists: This is the stage most people think 'the startup' actually is — experts treat it as just one stage among several, arriving only after the idea has already been discovered, validated, planned, and proven.
stageRoles.whatShouldHappen: The founder builds the real deliverable end-to-end, applying everything decided in Planning and learned in Prototyping.
stageRoles.prerequisites: Planning complete; Prototyping complete or explicitly skipped.
stageRoles.whatComesNext: Testing & Refinement — a real build needs to be checked before it's exposed to real users at scale.
stageRoles.skipCondition: Never skippable — this is the stage that produces the actual product.
stageRoles.mandatoryReason: The core deliverable-producing stage every workspace must include.
stageRoles.folderGenerationGuidelines: One or more folders representing the actual components or workstreams the goal's domain requires to build — never invented components the goal doesn't imply.
stageRoles.fileGenerationGuidelines: Application role dominant — this stage is about producing the real thing, not learning concepts.
stageRoles.checklistGenerationPhilosophy: Tasks should build toward one complete, real deliverable.

stageRoles.purpose: Find and fix what's broken, weak, or unclear before real users depend on it.
stageRoles.whyThisStageExists: Experts never launch what hasn't been tested — this stage exists specifically to catch failures while the cost of fixing them is still low.
stageRoles.whatShouldHappen: The founder tests the real build against realistic use, fixes what fails, and tightens anything unclear or fragile.
stageRoles.prerequisites: Build stage complete — there must be a real thing to test.
stageRoles.whatComesNext: Launch — once quality is confirmed, the product is ready to be exposed to real users.
stageRoles.skipCondition: Not skippable — even a lightweight pass must occur before Launch.
stageRoles.mandatoryReason: Launch without this stage risks shipping avoidable failures to real users.
stageRoles.folderGenerationGuidelines: One folder covering the specific testing/QA activities the goal's domain calls for.
stageRoles.fileGenerationGuidelines: Validation role dominant — this stage exists to confirm quality, not add new functionality.
stageRoles.checklistGenerationPhilosophy: Tasks should find and fix problems, not add new scope.

stageRoles.purpose: Expose the finished, tested product to real users and complete the goal the user set out to achieve.
stageRoles.whyThisStageExists: A product that's never launched has no real-world outcome — experts treat launch as its own deliberate stage, not an afterthought once building is 'done'.
stageRoles.whatShouldHappen: The founder executes the specific steps needed to make the product available and known to its intended users.
stageRoles.whatComesNext: Growth & Optimization — after launch, the focus shifts from shipping to sustaining and improving.
stageRoles.skipCondition: Never skippable — this is the stage the goal is literally measured against.
stageRoles.mandatoryReason: Without this stage the workspace never explicitly closes the loop on the user's stated goal.
stageRoles.folderGenerationGuidelines: Should map directly to the literal launch activities the goal implies — the least abstract stage, and should read as clearly goal-specific.
stageRoles.fileGenerationGuidelines: Application and Validation roles dominate — executing the launch and confirming it actually happened.
stageRoles.checklistGenerationPhilosophy: Tasks should be the final, concrete steps to actually ship.

stageRoles.purpose: Sustain and improve the product after launch based on real usage.
stageRoles.whyThisStageExists: Experts know launch is a beginning, not an end — ongoing iteration based on real feedback is what separates products that survive from ones that don't.
stageRoles.whatShouldHappen: The founder establishes an ongoing habit of reviewing real usage and feedback and making targeted improvements.
stageRoles.whatComesNext: None — terminal stage. May loop back into a new Discovery cycle for the next opportunity.
stageRoles.skipCondition: Skippable for short-timeframe or narrowly-scoped goals where post-launch growth isn't in scope.
stageRoles.mandatoryReason: Valuable for long-horizon goals, optional for narrowly-scoped ones.
stageRoles.folderGenerationGuidelines: One folder focused on ongoing improvement, tied to the goal's domain — forward-looking, not a repeat of Build or Testing.
stageRoles.fileGenerationGuidelines: A Validation-role file (reviewing real results) paired with an Application-role file (making the resulting improvement).
stageRoles.checklistGenerationPhilosophy: Tasks should be ongoing and habitual, driven by real feedback rather than one-time.

stageRules.orderEnforcement: Stages must be customized and emitted in the exact order defined in stageRoles — never reordered, even if the model believes a different order fits the goal better.
stageRules.stageToFolderMapping: Each mandatory or included stage becomes one or more folders. A stage never becomes zero folders unless it was explicitly skipped per its canBeSkipped rule.
stageRules.compressionRule: For small workspace tiers, adjacent optional stages may be merged into a single folder rather than omitted, so the execution arc stays intact even when folder count is limited.
stageRules.expansionRule: For large workspace tiers, a single stage may expand into multiple folders (e.g. one per component or workstream) but must never spawn folders that belong to a different stage's purpose.
stageRules.renamingRule: The abstract stage role label (e.g. 'Discovery', 'Build') must NEVER appear as a folder name in generated output — it must always be rewritten into language specific to the user's actual goal.
stageRules.skipRule: A stage may only be omitted entirely if its canBeSkipped is true AND the goal or clarification answers give a specific reason (e.g. problem already validated, no prototype needed) — never omitted by default.

folderGenerationRules.namingPhilosophy: Folder names must be outcome-shaped and goal-specific, never generic labels.
folderGenerationRules.noDuplicateFolders: No two folders may cover the same ground, even if their source stage roles differ.
folderGenerationRules.noInventedContent: Never invent a folder for a product type, feature, or activity not actually implied by the user's goal — every folder must trace back to a specific line of reasoning from the goal text plus exactly one blueprint stage role.
folderGenerationRules.orderMustMatchStageOrder: Folders must appear in the same order as their source stage roles.
folderGenerationRules.folderCountTarget: Total folder count must respect the size tier's target range supplied at generation time — use stageRules.compressionRule / expansionRule to hit it, never by inventing unrelated folders.
folderGenerationRules.oneStageOneReasonPerFolder: Every folder must be traceable to exactly one stage role — a folder must never straddle two stages' purposes.

fileRoleDefinitions.Introduction: Frames why this folder's work matters and what 'done' looks like — no deep content yet.
fileRoleDefinitions.Concept: Defines the underlying idea, plan, or hypothesis the folder's work requires.
fileRoleDefinitions.Hands-on Practice: A structured, guided activity applying the concept in a low-stakes way (e.g. a small test or rough draft).
fileRoleDefinitions.Application: Real, goal-relevant work — not a drill, an actual deliverable.
fileRoleDefinitions.Validation: Confirms the folder's work is actually correct, complete, or ready for the next stage.

fileGenerationRules.roleSelectionRule: Not every folder needs all 5 roles — use the source stage role's fileGenerationGuidelines to decide which roles actually apply. Fewer, well-chosen roles is better than forcing all 5.
fileGenerationRules.namingRule: File titles must be renamed from the abstract role into goal-specific language — the role name itself must never appear as the file title.
fileGenerationRules.noDuplicateRolesUnlessJustified: A folder should not repeat the same file role twice unless the goal genuinely requires two distinct pieces of that kind of work.

checklistGenerationRules.philosophy: Every checklist exists to move the file's stated goal toward real completion — never to demonstrate knowledge for its own sake.
rules: Follow logical order — each task's output should be usable by the next task.
Avoid vague wording such as 'plan for X' or 'think about Y'.
Avoid duplicating work already covered by an earlier file's checklist.
Every task must build toward completing that file's stated objective.
checklistGenerationRules.notice: This section defines HOW checklists must be generated. It must never be used as a source of literal checklist text — no task here is meant to be copied into a generated workspace.

structuralChecks: No duplicate folder names in the generated workspace.
No duplicate file titles within the same folder.
No empty folders — every folder must contain at least one file.
Folder order matches the blueprint's stage order.
Every mandatory stage (isMandatory: true) is present at least once.
Total folder count falls within the requested size tier's target range.
Every file maps to exactly one declared file role.
No abstract blueprint label (stage role or file role name) appears verbatim in any generated folder or file title.
contentChecks: No product type, platform, or technology is mentioned that isn't implied by the user's actual goal.
Every non-stub file's checklist complies with checklistGenerationRules.
Checklist tasks within a file contain no duplicates and no vague wording.
validationRules.enforcement: Phase 1 status: these rules are declarative only. They describe what a valid output must satisfy so a future validation pass (code-level check or a model self-check step) can verify them — they are not yet enforced by any code path.

generationConstraints.blueprintIsReasoningAidOnly: This entire document exists to shape HOW the AI thinks about structuring the workspace. No field in this document — stage names, role names, guideline text, or example verbs — should ever be copied verbatim into generated folder names, file names, descriptions, or checklist items.
generationConstraints.tokenEfficiencyRule: Prefer reusing this blueprint's structure over re-deriving an execution shape from scratch for every prompt — this is the mechanism that reduces hallucination and token usage across hundreds of different product/startup goals.
generationConstraints.customizationRequirement: Every stage role and file role must be fully renamed into language specific to the user's actual goal before appearing in any output shown to the user.
